newsitem.title: USA: SWIMMING-BENNETT WINS TWO EVENTS AT U.S. NATIONALS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-BENNETT WINS TWO EVENTS AT U.S. NATIONALS.

text.p: Olympic gold medalist Brooke Bennett won her second event of the Phillips 66 U.S. National Swimming Championships on Saturday.
Bennett, 16, America's newest distance queen after winning the 800 freestyle title at the Atlanta Games, won her third consecutive 400-meter freestyle title in four minutes, 12.14 seconds.
Bennett won the 800 title Wednesday. Bennett has won the last three national titles in both the 400 and 800 events, and has not lost a race since the March 1996 Olympic Trials.
"It's nice being on top but it's such a different feeling to have everyone chasing after you," Bennett said. "Two years ago I was doing the chasing."
It was a good night for U.S. Olympians on Day 4 of the 5-day meet, the first major meet since the Olympic Games in Atlanta.
Beth Botsford, 15, the 1996 Olympic gold medalist in the 100-meter backstroke, won her third national title in the event in 1:01.94.
Tripp Schwenk, the 1996 Olympic silver medalist in the 200 backstroke, won the 100 backstroke in 55.82. Schwenk, 25, is one of the oldest swimmers in the field.
Schoolgirl Amanda Beard,15, won the 100-meter breastroke in 1:09.97. She also won the 200-meter breaststroke earlier in the week.
Beard, Olympic silver medalist in both events, has only been swimming a month since having a cyst removed from her right wrist.
Kurt Grote, an Olympic gold medalist on the medley relay team, won the 100 breastroke in 1:02.73.
The only non-Olympians to win were Californian Chad Carvin, schoolgirl Misty Hyman and teenager Nate Dusing.

The 22-year-old Carvin won his third event in his first major meet since recovering from cardiomyopathy, a virus that attacks the heart muscle. A sure-lock for the Olympic team, Carvin was forced to drop out of the March, 1996, Olympic Trials. Carvin also won the 200 freestyle and 400 individual medley events.
Hyman, 17, won the 100 butterfly in 59.14, which would have won her a silver medal at the Olympics.
Dusing, 18, won the men's 100 butterfly in 53.99.
